---
title: "Using a template"
subtitle: "Copy one file, replace one block, rewrite the slides."
description: "How to take a carousel template out of the gallery and turn it into your own release deck."
---

A template is a single Typst file.
It imports nothing and depends on no package, so a copy of it is complete.

## What you need

[Typst](https://typst.app/docs) and the fonts the template names.

If you already have [Quarto](https://quarto.org), you have Typst: `quarto typst` runs the copy it ships, and takes the same arguments as the commands below.

The gallery vendors its fonts so that a clone renders identically anywhere.
If you work inside a clone, point Typst at them:

```bash
typst compile --font-path fonts --ignore-system-fonts carousel.typ carousel.pdf
```

If you copy a template into your own project instead, install the fonts it names, or change the three font bindings to families you already have.
Typst reports a missing family as a warning and carries on with a fallback face, so a deck can compile cleanly and still be set in the wrong type.
Read the output, do not just read the exit code.

## Copy it

Take the whole directory, or just the file:

```bash
curl -O https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mcanouil/typst-carousel-gallery/main/templates/editorial/drop-cap/carousel.typ
```

Every template's page has a download link for the same file.

## Replace the project block

The top of every file carries the only part you have to change:

```typst
// --- PROJECT (replace these) ---
#let project = "Acme Kit"
#let version = "2.1.0"
#let repo-url = "https://github.com/mcanouil/typst-carousel-gallery"
#let date = "2026-01-01"
```

Change the document title on the line above it too.

## Rewrite the slides

Under `// --- SLIDES ---` there are six blocks, in this order: a cover, four content slides, and a closing slide with the links.
Keep the shape and change the words.

Two rules are worth keeping even when you change everything else.

Body text stays at 14 pt or larger, because a slide has to survive being shown at about 250 pixels wide in a feed.
Every URL a reader can see stays wrapped in `#link()`, because a bare URL in a PDF is dead text they would have to retype.

The [reference](reference.qmd) lists the bindings and helpers every template shares, so you know what a name means before you change it.

## Change the palette

The theme block binds eight colours.
Swapping those eight is usually enough to move a deck onto a different palette without touching a single slide:

```typst
// --- THEME ---
#let ground = rgb("#f6f1e7")   // page fill
#let paper = rgb("#fffdf7")    // light panel
#let ink = rgb("#221d16")      // body text
#let muted = rgb("#7a6f5d")    // secondary text
#let hair = rgb("#d9cdb5")     // rules and borders
#let accent = rgb("#b5830a")   // the one accent
#let slab = rgb("#221d16")     // code background
#let slab-fg = rgb("#f0e7d5")  // code foreground
```

## Build it

```bash
typst compile carousel.typ carousel.pdf
```

For the images the platforms prefer, ask Typst for one file per slide:

```bash
typst compile --format png --ppi 144 carousel.typ 'slide-{p}.png'
```

Then look at every slide before posting.
A clean compile only proves the page did not overflow.
Content inside a fixed-height block draws straight over the footer and still exits 0.
